subject: Request: quarterly invoicing + extended payment terms for pilot
messages:
From: Caroline Sunstone <caroline.sunstone@sunstonehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@sunstonehealth.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing cadence for 6-month pilot / PO attached

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the team is excited to kick off the pilot. Procurement asked me to confirm invoicing cadence and payment terms before we sign. They typically issue POs on a quarterly basis for pilot engagements and would prefer to receive invoices quarterly (one invoice per quarter) with Net-90 terms on payment.

I attached a PO stub (Sunstone_PO_2026Q3.pdf) for your reference. From our side, quarterly billing reduces AP overhead and the Net-90 reflects their internal payment cycle. Can Redwood accept quarterly invoices with Net-90 for this pilot? If Net-90 isn’t feasible, would Net-60 be an option?

We’re trying to avoid upfront prepayment if possible; let me know what approvals you need and any documentation (SOW redline, procurement contact) we should return.

Appreciate your help — happy to hop on a quick call if useful.

Best,
Caroline Sunstone
Director, Strategic Procurement
Sunstone Health

Attachment: Sunstone_PO_2026Q3.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Caroline Sunstone <caroline.sunstone@sunstonehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing cadence for 6-month pilot / PO attached

Hi Caroline — thanks for sending the PO and for outlining Sunstone’s preferences. We’re excited to partner on the pilot. Two quick points:

1) Redwood’s standard terms for new pilot customers are Net-30 with monthly invoicing (to keep cashflow predictable).
2) We can be flexible, but extended terms and quarterly invoicing require approval from finance + revenue operations because they change revenue recognition and increase credit exposure.

I’ve attached a redline of the SOW showing the pilot scope (SOW-Redline-Sunstone.docx). I’ll start the approval thread internally now, and circle back with a concrete option. Preliminary ask: would you accept Net-60 with quarterly invoicing as a middle ground if we can’t get Net-90 approved?

I’ll follow up by Monday with the decision and any conditions (e.g., PO on file, single invoice per quarter, and a short-term credit check).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec approval request: Sunstone pilot — quarterly invoicing + Net-90? (DE-4921)

Team,

Looping you in for an approval decision. Sunstone Health (Strategic procurement) is ready to sign a 6-month pilot (anticipated ARR run rate $180k/year if converted) but requests quarterly invoicing and Net-90 payment terms. PO attached from their side.

Why this matters:
- Revenue impact: pilot value ~ $90k over 6 months; potential expansion to enterprise could be material (healthcare vertical).
- Risk: Net-90 increases DSO and credit exposure; quarterly invoices reduce invoice cadence which affects cashflow forecasting.
- Precedent: We occasionally grant Net-60 for enterprise customers with credit-reviewed contracts; Net-90 is rare and typically requires a contract-level exception + approval from RevOps and Finance leadership.

My recommendation: Approve quarterly invoicing + Net-60 for the 6-month pilot on these conditions:
- PO on file before first invoice (they already provided it)
- One invoice per quarter (no split invoices)
- No discount beyond the pilot promotional discount already discussed (5% list); no further pricing concessions tied to terms
- Credit hold if payment > Net-60 + 30 days (i.e., escalation to collections)

If we must offer Net-90 to close, I recommend requiring an upfront 30% deposit on the first quarter invoice (to mitigate cash exposure) and explicit exec sign-off on the legal exception.

Attachments: Sunstone_PO_2026Q3.pdf, SOW-Redline-Sunstone.docx

Asks: Rafael/Vivek — can you confirm whether the Net-60 compromise is acceptable from credit and revenue recognition perspectives, and whether the deposit requirement for Net-90 is workable? Neha — FYI for renewal/expansion planning.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 10:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exec approval request: Sunstone pilot — quarterly invoicing + Net-90? (DE-4921)

Marissa / team,

I reviewed the ask and ran a quick credit check (no red flags, annual spend profile moderate). Finance position: we are willing to approve quarterly invoicing + Net-60 for the 6-month pilot under the conditions you proposed. Details: 

- Approve: quarterly invoicing + Net-60.
- If customer insists on Net-90, approve only if there is a 30% upfront deposit on the first invoice and an explicit Legal/Exec exception noted on the contract.
- No additional discounts tied to payment terms.
- Require PO before first invoice and add a note to the invoice referencing the PO number for AP reconciliation.

Operational notes (Vivek): we’ll flag the deal in RevOps so billing can schedule one invoice per quarter and set up reminder workflows. Collections will have an automated escalation at 60 + 30 days.

Rafael Mendes
Sr. Director, Finance — Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Caroline Sunstone <caroline.sunstone@sunstonehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@sunstonehealth.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing cadence for 6-month pilot / PO attached

Hi Caroline — quick update and thanks for your patience. Finance approved a compromise that I think works for both sides:

- Redwood can accept quarterly invoicing for the 6-month pilot.
- Payment terms: Net-60.
- If Sunstone requires Net-90, we can accept that only with a 30% upfront deposit on the first invoice and Exec/Legal exception noted on the contract.
- PO on file is required before we issue the first invoice (we have the stub you sent).

Next steps: I can update the SOW and contract language to reflect Net-60 and quarterly invoicing and send the redline (SOW-Redline-Sunstone.docx) and a DocuSign link for signature. If you confirm Net-90 + 30% deposit, we’ll include the deposit clause and route for exec sign-off prior to countersignature.

Which option would you like to proceed with? Happy to schedule a quick call to finalize today if that helps.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: SOW-Redline-Sunstone.docx
